---
title: "RPSA Model Four Scoring-Scale Sensitivity Analysis"
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document: default
params:
  data_file: RPSA4.xls
---

## Objective

Assess whether the 26-point maximum for Model Four affects comparisons with
Models One through Three, which each have a 25-point maximum. The sensitivity
analysis multiplies Model Four scores by 25/26 without rounding. This preserves
component weights relative to one another and preserves the ordering of tracts
within Model Four.

## Data

To knit, install `readxl`, `knitr`, and `rmarkdown` if needed. Place
`RPSA4.xls` next to this file or set the `data_file` parameter to the workbook
path, relative to this file or absolute.

```{r data}
model_columns <- paste0("RPSA", 1:4)
workbook <- readxl::read_excel("/Users/madelineratoza/Desktop/RPSA4.xls")
stopifnot(all(model_columns %in% names(workbook)))
scores <- workbook[model_columns]
stopifnot(all(vapply(scores, is.numeric, logical(1))))

original <- as.matrix(scores[complete.cases(scores), ])
stopifnot(nrow(original) >= 2L, all(is.finite(original)),
          all(original == trunc(original)))
data.frame(
  Total = nrow(scores),
  Included = nrow(original),
  Excluded = nrow(scores) - nrow(original)
) |> knitr::kable()
```

## Statistical comparisons

Both analyses use the same complete tracts. Friedman tests compare the four
scores within tracts. Two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests use a
normal approximation with continuity correction and Bonferroni adjustment across
all six pairs for each scale. Positive differences indicate that the second
model in a pair scores higher on average.

```{r tests}
# Work in units of 1/26 point to preserve exact ties in the rank tests.
original_units <- 26 * original
rescaled_units <- original_units
rescaled_units[, "RPSA4"] <- 25 * original[, "RPSA4"]

analyze_scores <- function(score_units) {
  friedman <- stats::friedman.test(score_units)
  pairs <- utils::combn(colnames(score_units), 2, simplify = FALSE)
  pairwise <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(pair) {
    difference <- score_units[, pair[2]] - score_units[, pair[1]]
    test <- stats::wilcox.test(difference, exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE)

    data.frame(
      Comparison = paste(pair[2], "minus", pair[1]),
      Mean_difference = mean(difference) / 26,
      Median_difference = median(difference) / 26,
      P = test$p.value
    )
  }))
  pairwise$Adjusted_p <- stats::p.adjust(pairwise$P, method = "bonferroni")

  list(
    omnibus = data.frame(
      Chi_squared = unname(friedman$statistic),
      DF = unname(friedman$parameter),
      P = friedman$p.value
    ),
    pairwise = pairwise
  )
}

original_results <- analyze_scores(original_units)
rescaled_results <- analyze_scores(rescaled_units)
```

### Friedman tests

```{r friedman-table}
format_p <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)

omnibus <- rbind(
  cbind(Scale = "Original", original_results$omnibus),
  cbind(Scale = "Common 25-point maximum", rescaled_results$omnibus)
)
omnibus$P <- format_p(omnibus$P)
knitr::kable(omnibus, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Scale", "Chi-squared", "df", "p"))
```

### Paired Wilcoxon tests

```{r pairwise-table}
pairwise <- rbind(
  cbind(Scale = "Original", original_results$pairwise),
  cbind(Scale = "Common 25-point maximum", rescaled_results$pairwise)
)
pairwise$P <- format_p(pairwise$P)
pairwise$Adjusted_p <- format_p(pairwise$Adjusted_p)
knitr::kable(
  pairwise, digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Scale", "Comparison", "Mean difference (points)",
                "Median difference (points)", "p", "Bonferroni-adjusted p")
)
```

## Interpretation

Interpret the paired tests alongside the magnitude and direction of the score
differences. The sensitivity analysis addresses the overall scoring scale.
Assessing the influence of individual indicators or weights would require
separate model specifications.
